title: Reduced-fidelity refusal advises a larger STEP facet budget when a face's evaluation cap kept the coarser mesh

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

body:
What happens: since #1568 (PR #1578), a STEP refinement pass that runs past `FACE_EVAL_CAP` on a face proven continuous keeps the coarser mesh, and the import carries the usual reduced-fidelity chord. The refusals and notes built from that chord (`model_fidelity::TOO_COARSE`, `crates/app/src/model_fidelity.rs:58`, and the per-operation refusal at `:311`, plus the note at `:270`) all say "re-import with a larger STEP facet budget". When the evaluation cap is the cause, a larger budget changes nothing: the same face runs out again.

Where it stands: `step_refine::Kept` now carries `eval_capped`, and the import's log line names the cause (PR #1578). The cause stops at `parse_with_chord_budget`, which returns only `(Mesh, f64)`; `schema::ReducedFidelity` stores only `chord_mm`, and it is saved with the project.

Expected: when the coarser mesh was kept because of the evaluation cap, the user-facing text says so (e.g. "a face needed more than N evaluations to refine; re-export the model or import an STL") instead of advising a larger budget.

Needs: the cause carried out of the importer, a field on `ReducedFidelity` (or a sibling component) that rides copies, undo and save, and a project-format bump with a loader default.

No corpus file reaches this path today (M5's 76-file corpus, review of PR #1578).

Found while fixing the review of PR #1578 (#1568).

Done means: a model whose mesh was kept by the evaluation-cap fallback gets a refusal/note that names the cap, not the facet budget, pinned by a test; budget-limited imports keep today's wording.
